basics.name: Xianglei Fang
basics.summary: Physics Ph.D. student at William & Mary

work.position: Fixed-Target Acceptance Studies for the ePIC Detector at the EIC
work.summary: Conducted DD4hep/Geant4-based full detector simulations for the ePIC experiment in the fixed-target (FXT) configuration, focusing on acceptance and performance studies relevant to low-energy QCD and baryon-rich matter.
highlights: Supervisor: Prof. Helen Caines & Prof. Laura Havener (Yale University)

work.position: 2+1 Dimensional Stochastic Relativistic Viscous Hydrodynamics from the Metropolis algorithm
work.summary: Numerical simulations of relativistic hydrodynamics and their applications in high-energy nuclear physics.
highlights: Supervisor: Prof. Derek Teaney (Stony Brook University)

work.position: The Stochastic Relativistic Advection Diffusion Equation From the Metropolis Algorithm
work.summary: Developing and utilizing advanced numerical techniques, such as the Metropolis algorithm, to simulate advection-diffusion dynamics and thermal noise in relativistic systems.
highlights: Supervisor: Prof. Derek Teaney (Stony Brook University)
